author: potuz
content: Unfortunately, from the point of view of the protocol, the relay "is the builder". The node can't distinguish between a single endpoint serving many indices from the same builder and serving different builders. Moreover, with optimistic relaying that relay is indeed broadcasting a payload without any guarantees of it being valid. Builders that participate in such a relay with untrusted builders would be sharing the risk. And just in case this wasn't clear in my post, if builders 1 and 2 where served on endpoint X and builders 2 and 3 where served on endpoint Y, on a payload failure from 2 we'll block endpoints X **and** Y, and also mark indices 1,2 and 3 for an epoch

author: potuz
content: Builders are free to have their own unshared endpoint

author: potuz
content: And be responsible for their own actions

author: 0xunclebill
content:
if a builder is part of a relay but also is directly connected to proposers and via the direct connection a payload is missed, based on your proposal do we:

ban just the builder
OR
ban the builder and the relay it was associated with

author: potuz
content: Both, that's the whole point. We don't really know what happens behind a relay, the indices can be rotated by the relay itself or belong to each individual builder for example

author: potuz
content: So we can only ban it as a whole
